newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares rise, seen tracking Wall Street.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares rise, seen tracking Wall Street.

text.p: The Warsaw bourse extended Tuesday's gain shadowing Dow Jones performance and local speculators were seen tracking Wall Street in the absence of clear fundamental signals from their own turf.

The main market's WIG index rose 243 points, or 1.5 percent, to 16,281.5, and turnover was virtually flat at 174.3 million zlotys ($58 million) on all three markets as 76 issues rose, six fell and 11 were flat.

Analysts said that even though there was limited short-term flow of funds between Warsaw and main foreign exchanges recent world swings offered domestic players a chance to cash in on rapid changes of mood.
"Daily Dow Jones changes influence WIG and it's hard to tell when such strong connection will end," said Pawel Tarnowski of Raiffeisen Capital and Investment Polska.
Some analysts said in the next several weeks the Warsaw bourse was likely to suffer from capital drawn by some attractive primary market offers and forthcoming elections.

Paper firm Celuloza currently offers shares of at least 112.5 million zlotys ($37.5 million) on the primary market and next week metals trader Impexmetal SA will start its at least 222-million-zloty ($74 million) offer.
Analysts saw limited impact of March lower-than-expected 0.8 percent month-on-month CPI figure, released on Tuesday, as no rate-cut was seen in the first half of the year.
Debt-ridden construction firm Espebepe extended Tuesday's surge, rising 9.1 percent on hopes that the firm would convince its creditors to accept its new restructuring programme.
